name: supervised_position_v1 (position control for stage 2 of the supervised/calibrated work plan, 2026-11-01)
frozen_at: 2026-11-01, before any score of the new arms was computed
origin: Stage 2 (results/supervised_budget_v1): LR17 beat AUTO on PRMBench from ~50 labels and the Qwen PRMs on Socratic from ~50 labels. Its Socratic within-answer gain over AUTO was +.11 to +.17, and step position alone has within-AUC .731 on Socratic (Step 481). Omri approved this check on 2026-11-01.
question: Is the supervised gain explained by step position? Does an LR on [PRM, position] match LR17, and does LR17 gain from adding position?
access: CPU only, stored per-step scores, no new inference. Same k-label in-domain access as stage 2.
design: Identical to stage 2: same groups, the same R = 20 splits and label draws (seed 20261101 + rep), same budgets, same LR (C = 1 fixed, balanced). The stage-2 module budget.py is imported unchanged.
position_feature: relative position within the answer, (i + 0.5) / n_steps (common.relative_position). A single linear term; a non-linear position shape is not tested here.

arms.LR17: as stage 2, refitted; must reproduce stage 2's BUDGET.csv exactly (parity gate)
arms.POSONLY: relpos itself as a score (no labels), reported as a reference

metrics: on the test half: PRMScore under GAP and mean within-answer AUC
summary: as stage 2: per bench x PRM x k mean, 2.5/97.5 percentiles across repetitions and count of positive repetitions; k* as stage 2.

predeclared_readings.P1: Socratic, all of the pool: LR17 - POS2 PRMScore mean > 0 and positive in >= 16/20 repetitions, in >= 2 of the 3 strong PRMs. Met = LR17's Socratic gain is not explained by linear position alone.
predeclared_readings.P2: Socratic, all of the pool: LR18 - LR17 PRMScore mean <= +0.5 in >= 2 of the 3 strong PRMs. Met = the channels already carry what linear position adds.
predeclared_readings.P3: PRMBench, all of the pool: LR17 - POS2 PRMScore mean > 0 and positive in >= 16/20 repetitions in >= 3 of 4 PRMs.
predeclared_readings.note: Readings, not method gates. If P1 fails, the Socratic claim of stage 2 must be reported as possibly a position effect of the benchmark's construction.

caveats: Variation across repetitions is not a CI for one fixed test set.
